service_boundary: Represents the developer inference API Meta operates at api.meta.ai, not the consumer Meta AI assistant, the Muse Code coding agent, individual Muse or Llama model releases, or open-weight Muse Glimmer running on customer hardware.
regional_controls: Availability is jurisdiction-gated by a dated Model Designation and Geographic Use Policy that names restricted territories and per-model country exclusions, and Meta may enable or restrict any jurisdiction at its discretion. Meta states it does not receive, determine, or route traffic based on end-user location, and no customer-selected processing region, regional endpoint, or private networking option is documented.
retention_controls: Data handling is tied to a published model tier rather than an account setting. Standard-tier models are processed under the Meta Global Processor Terms and are not used to train Meta models; the discounted Contributor tier grants Meta permission to train on prompts and completions, carries an instruction not to submit confidential or personal information, and offers no per-request opt-out. Meta retains content and usage data to deliver the service, meet legal obligations, exercise its rights, and run safety, abuse, and policy review; no zero-retention or customer deletion control is documented.
routing: Customers select a published Meta model id; the service exposes only Meta's own hosted models and performs no cross-provider routing or fallback.
customization: No fine-tuning, customer-supplied models, or dedicated deployments are documented. Lifecycle control is limited to pinning published checkpoint model ids and to prompt caching.
strengths: Three interchangeable request formats run the same models over one pipeline, so existing OpenAI or Anthropic client code ports with a base-URL and key change.
Training use is bound to an explicitly labelled model id and backed by processor terms, a data security addendum, and a published subprocessor list, rather than to an account toggle.
An unauthenticated status endpoint reports overall service state, per-model health, and recent incident history alongside documented retry guidance.
tradeoffs: The terms govern a limited preview period, and there is no batch, reserved-capacity, dedicated-endpoint, or fine-tuning path.
Regional control is a restriction list rather than a customer choice: no processing geography, regional endpoint, or private-network option is offered.
Only Meta's own hosted models are served, and account administration is limited to team-scoped API keys and shared rate limits with no documented SSO, audit logging, or service-level commitment.
